06. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner, learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the informant.
2. The Petitioner is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with Cuttack Mahila P.S. Case No.103 of 2024 for commission of offences punishable under Sections 376/511/385/506 of IPC.

entities.text: Cuttack Mahila P.S. Case No.103 of 2024
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3. Perused the 164 of Cr.P.C. statement of the victim.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioner referring to Annexure-2 submits that similar allegations were made in an F.I.R. instituted on 22.06.2024 at Bangalore (Annexure-5), which was registered as H.A.L. Police Station Case No.524 of 2024.

entities.text: H.A.L. Police Station Case No.524 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that relating to the said P.S.Case, the petitioner was released on bail by order dated 24.06.2024, vide Annexure-2.
Referring to the same, it is further submitted that exaggerated allegations have been made against the petitioner, in respect of which the present anticipatory bail application has been filed.
5. Learned counsel for the State as well as informant opposed the prayer for bail.

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the informant submits that the F.I.R. at Bangalore did not disclose any allegation under Section 376 of IPC, which is clearly made out in the case at hand.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled to be released on pre-arrest bail.
Learned counsel also refers to the statements of the victim and her friends and reiterates such submission.
7. This Court perused the 164 of Cr.P.C. statement of the victim, in which she has referred to the earlier case at Bangalore.

On a conspectus of materials on record including the statement of the friends of the victim and the background, in which the allegation is made in the case at hand, this Court directs that on surrendering, the petitioner shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as would be fixed by the learned Court below.

It is needless to say that the petitioner shall not threaten or intimidate the informant and her family members and in the event of any threat perception, it will be open to the prosecution as well as the informant to seek variance of this order.
8. Accordingly, the ABLAPL stands disposed of.
9.
Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
